# Design Grill

An optional pre-lock design-pressure step inside the **DESIGN** phase. It resolves design
dependencies one question at a time before a `DESIGN_LOCK_ID` is written, and records the
result as a durable artifact so downstream agents inherit the decisions.

This step adds **no mechanical gate**. Nothing here is linted and `GRILL_LOCK` is not a
relay phase or a relay field — it is a durable design sub-artifact. The phase boundaries,
dispatch tokens, and merge gate in the role skills' adjacent `protocol.md` are unchanged and remain the only
enforced surfaces. Grilling is a human-alignment tool, not an authority or evidence gate;
it does not substitute for any mechanical artifact.

## When to run it

Record one line in the design record:

```text
GRILL_REQUIRED: <yes | no>
```

`yes` when any of these is true:
- the operator explicitly asked to be grilled;
- new-feature / `still-open` work at medium ceremony tier or above;
- ambiguous product semantics;
- a cross-domain boundary contract;
- a hard-to-reverse data / API / model decision;
- multiple downstream decisions depend on one unsettled choice.

Otherwise `no` — skip it. This step is never mandatory; the protocol's existing ceremony
pressure already scales effort to stakes, so do not grill tiny/small fixes or
`already-closed`/promote-existing work.

## How to run it

Use the interview behavior from the vendored `grill-me` skill
(`vendor/mattpocock/grill-me/SKILL.md`, MIT © 2026 Matt Pocock):

- ask the questions **one at a time**;
- walk each branch of the design tree, resolving dependencies between decisions before
  moving on;
- for every question, give your **recommended** answer;
- if a question can be answered by inspecting the codebase, inspect it instead of asking
  the operator.

## What it must produce — the GRILL_LOCK artifact

A grill that stays in chat does not survive this protocol: downstream agents inherit only
durable artifacts. End the grill by writing a `GRILL_LOCK` and folding it into the design
record so the `DESIGN_LOCK_ID` that feeds the plan carries the resolved decisions.

```text
GRILL_LOCK_ID: <id>
GRILL_REQUIRED: yes
GRILL_SOURCE:
- plan/design/audit relay read:
- code/docs inspected:
- questions answered from codebase:
- questions asked operator:

Resolved decisions:
- <decision> — answer — reason — source <code | operator | default>

Rejected alternatives:
- <alternative> — reason rejected

Still operator-owned:
- <question> — why it cannot be inferred

Design-lock impact:
- <what must be reflected in DESIGN_LOCK_ID / spec / plan>
```

Reference `GRILL_LOCK_ID` from the `DESIGN_LOCK_ID` it feeds. The grill never writes
`CONTEXT.md` — that filename carries domain-glossary or implementation-decision meaning in
other ecosystems and would conflict; this package's design artifact is the `GRILL_LOCK`,
folded into `DESIGN_LOCK_ID`.
